subject: Petrichor AI — on-prem cluster, node pools & storage alignment
messages:
From: Leo Chen <leo.chen@petrichorai.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@petrichorai.com
Date: 2029-05-12T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem deployment — quick ask on cluster and storage sizing

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking this — we’re evaluating Redwood for an on-prem inference deployment at Petrichor. We have two sites (primary: us-west-2 datacenter; DR: us-east-1 colo) and plan to run inference-only clusters for production traffic, plus a small batch-training pool for fine-tuning.

Can you confirm the following at a high level so we can scope HW and procurement?
- Typical recommendation for node counts (per 1k QPS target), and a sample node pool split (inference vs aux/batching).
- Storage mix: local NVMe for caches vs network blockstore for model weights and checkpoints — suggested sizes and IOPS targets.
- Encryption & backups expectations (we need KMS integration and snapshot cadence ideas).
- Any preflight checks Redwood expects from our networking (eg NAT/GW, outbound egress rules, peering requirements).

I attached our basic environment inventory (petrichor_cluster_requirements_v1.xlsx). Looking for a short call this week to align.

Regards,
Leo Chen
Head of Infrastructure
Petrichor AI

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment — quick ask on cluster and storage sizing

Hi Leo — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the inventory — that helps. High-level answers below and we should kick off a 45m architecture review so we can follow up with a hands-on preflight checklist. Proposed times: Wed 5/15 10:00 PT or Thu 5/16 13:00 PT.

Quick answers:
- Node pools: For inference at ~1k QPS (typical LLM-sized requests, 1–2k token seq) we recommend a small fleet of GPU inference nodes in a 3-tier split:
  * Frontline (latency SLO): 3–5 smaller GPUs (eg A10/V100 equivalent) behind autoscaling to cover instant bursts and keep p99 latency low.
  * Bulk workers (throughput): 6–12 larger GPUs (A100-class) for steady throughput/ batching.
  * Auxiliary (batch training/ft): isolated node pool with separate network policy — no inference traffic on these nodes.
- Storage: NVMe (local) for KV cache and transient model shard caching (250–500GB per node recommended); network blockstore (encrypted) for model artifact store and checkpoints. Plan for blockstore with 10–20k IOPS for heavy model loads; many customers provision a mix of high IOPS for model weights + cheaper cold tiers for long-term checkpoints.
- Encryption & backups: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for disk keys. Snapshot cadence we commonly recommend: hourly for short retention caches (if needed), daily snapshots for models with weekly replication to DR.
- Networking: outbound egress to Redwood control plane must be allowed for telemetry and control-plane operations (or we can run a private control plane if required). Also prepare for load-balancer IP ranges, and allow mTLS between node pools.

I’ve looped in Dev (serving runtime) and Grace (deploy ops) — they’ll propose specifics and a short preflight checklist.

Best,
Ava Chen

Subject: Re: On-prem deployment — quick ask on cluster and storage sizing

Ava / team — jotting down notes ahead of the call; pushing a minimal viable infra recommendation so procurement can get rough quotes:

1) Node sizing (per site, primary / DR):
   - Frontline (latency): 4 x GPU nodes (each with 1 x 80GB GPU or 2 x 40GB) — reserved, with burst capacity + autoscaler.
   - Bulk (throughput): 10 x GPU nodes (A100/80GB equiv) in a separate node pool for batching; larger batch sizes and KV offload.
   - Batch training: 2–3 nodes (can be smaller or spot-like) behind strict network isolation.

2) Storage topology:
   - Local NVMe (per node): 400GB NVMe (fast cache) mounted with ephemeral lifecycle; set eviction / cache warming policies for model shards.
   - Blockstore (network): replicated blockstore (Ceph/RBD or SAN) providing model artifacts; recommend minimum 50TB usable at start, with 20k IOPS sustained for hot sets.
   - Backups: point-in-time snapshots to offsite cold storage (S3-like) weekly; incremental daily snapshots for recent artifacts.

3) Networking & operations:
   - NAT egress to control-plane endpoints (we will share IP ranges).
   - Per-node mTLS and service identity via cert manager; RBAC to isolate inference pods from batch nodes.
   - Monitoring: per-token latency traces, node-level disk metrics, and KV miss rates.

4) Preflight checklist items for Petrichor:
   - BMC/IPMI reachability for nodes.
   - VLAN mapping and routing rules to allow cross-pod egress to the control plane.
   - KMS/HSM integration details and cert signing CA.
   - Storage: confirm RPO/RTO targets and preferred blockstore vendor (Ceph/AWS Outpost/SAN).

I’ll bring a short diagram (network-drawing-v2.png) to the call and propose an initial BOM.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Leo Chen <leo.chen@petrichorai.com>

Cc: ops@petrichorai.com, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-14T07:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment — quick ask on cluster and storage sizing

Thanks for the detailed notes — this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs before the 5/15 call: 
- For model artifacts we plan to keep two copies (primary site blockstore + weekly replicated cold copy in DR). Does Redwood require synchronous replication for the model store?
- For KMS: we use a cloud KMS with on-prem HSM proxy; is the Redwood agent compatible with hardware-backed keys or do you need a separate key wrap flow?
- Separation of inference vs training: we want hard tenancy (no shared GPUs) — your node pool split covers that, but confirm network egress policies so training jobs cannot reach inference metrics endpoints.

Also attaching a quick sketch of our proposed rack-level topology (network-drawing-v2.png).

Thanks — Leo

To: Leo Chen <leo.chen@petrichorai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-14T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem deployment — quick ask on cluster and storage sizing

Leo — all good clarifications. Short answers and next steps below.

- Replication: synchronous replication is not required for our serving runtime; we recommend asynchronous replication to DR to avoid write latency affecting inference. Daily consistency + weekly full replication is the typical pattern. If your RTO requires sub-minute failover, we can discuss a more complex sync approach.

- KMS/HSM: our agent supports cloud KMS via a proxy to HSMs; we also support customer-managed key wraps. We’ll need the HSM endpoint and a test key to validate key unwrap during preflight.

- Tenant separation: enforce via node selectors + strict NetworkPolicies; training node pools should have egress deny to metrics and inference-specific services. We’ll add a validation in the preflight checklist to run a synthetic policy test that verifies egress rules.

Action items (we’ll cover these on the 5/15 10:00 PT call):
  1) Redwood to share IP ranges + control-plane endpoint docs (Ava).
  2) Petrichor to provide KMS HSM test endpoint and a short inventory mapping for NVMe host diags (Leo).
  3) Dev to produce an initial BOM and cost estimate for node mixes (Dev).
  4) Grace to prepare preflight checklist and link to shared drive.

Proposed call time confirmed: 2029-05-15 10:00 PT — invite sent.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the call.

Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
